raw_data.title: Spontaneous slow waves index multiple dimensions of recovery in Disorders of Consciousness
raw_data.abstract: Whether and how residual awareness is expressed in patients with Disorders of Consciousness (DoC) depends on the severity of brain damage and the transient functional state of the cortex at assessment. Classically, DoC are associated with electroencephalographic (EEG) slowing, marked by high-amplitude slow waves, even during the day. Yet, slow waves are also a hallmark of healthy sleep, where they are thought to serve restorative functions and to help maintain network homeostasis. Here, we asked whether slow waves in DoC can provide insights into the severity of cortical dysfunction or, conversely, into the preservation of residual awareness and recovery potential, by characterizing their spatial, temporal and morphological properties. We analyzed 256-channel EEG recorded during the Local-Global auditory paradigm in 236 DoC patients, including 123 in Unresponsive Wakefulness Syndrome (UWS), 62 in a Minimally Conscious State minus (MCS-) and 29 in MCS plus (MCS+). High-amplitude slow waves were detected as local events, and their density, amplitude and slopes were quantified scalp-wide and channel-wise, by mean level and temporal variability across the recording. Slow-wave features were related to concurrent (Coma Recovery Scale-Revised - CRS-R, Local-Global paradigm) and follow-up (one-year Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended - GOS-E) assessments of consciousness and functional recovery. Associations with MRI-derived measures of cortical integrity and structural connectivity, and differences between anoxic and traumatic etiologies, were also examined. Slow waves were more frequent in less severe DoC patients (i.e., MCS) compared to UWS. Slow-wave slopes were also steeper frontally and increased at a faster rate in patients exhibiting higher levels of consciousness and/or markers of conscious access during the Local-Global paradigm. More frequent and steeper slow waves at baseline further predicted recovery of consciousness and of functional independence at one year. At the individual level, slow-wave features classified states of consciousness above chance (AUC = 0.62 and 0.71 for MCS- and MCS+ versus UWS), whereas outcome prediction remained modest (0.56-0.58). These clinical associations had a structural basis: slow-wave occurrence was greater after traumatic than anoxic injury and scaled with the integrity of subcortico-cortical projection fibers and consciousness-related cortical networks. Contrary to the classical view of delta activity as a non-specific marker of impaired consciousness, prominent spontaneous slow waves indexed behavioral and neurophysiological signs of awareness and better recovery. Beyond reflecting a propensity for pathological bistability, they may also signal the integrity of the networks required to generate them, together with their residual capacity for dynamic regulation.

raw_data.title: The Effective Visual Acuity of Butterflies in Flight
raw_data.abstract: The spatial visual acuity of an eye is determined by both the spatial sampling density of the retina and the angular sensitivity of individual photoreceptors. In insect compound eyes, these are respectively characterised by the interommatidial angle, {Delta}{varphi}, and photoreceptor acceptance angle, {Delta}{rho}. During movement, however, finite photoreceptor integration times cause retinal image motion to broaden the effective acceptance angle, potentially degrading spatial resolution beyond its anatomical limit. This problem is especially acute in flying insects, which experience large rotational velocities during locomotion and must actively stabilise gaze to limit retinal image motion. Butterflies present a particularly demanding case because their flight is characterised by large, wingbeat-coupled thoracic oscillations. Here, we quantify how gaze stabilisation limits motion blur in freely flying Monarch butterflies Danaus plexippus by combining free-flight kinematic reconstruction of the head and thorax with separate intracellular measurements of photoreceptor acceptance angles and integration times from quiescent butterflies. We found that, without head compensation, thoracic oscillations would broaden the effective photoreceptor acceptance angle from its quiescent value of 2.17{degrees} to 9.38{degrees} during take-off. Compensatory head movements substantially reduced this motion-induced broadening, limiting the effective acceptance angle to 5.28{degrees}. Nevertheless, this 2.4-fold broadening of effective photoreceptor acceptance angle represents a substantial degradation of spatial acuity in flight, highlighting motion blur as an important constraint on the visual ecology of flying butterflies.

raw_data.title: Intracranial electrophysiology reveals distinct neural representations of nociception and salience in the human brain
raw_data.abstract: Neuroimaging studies have shown close overlap between neural representations of nociceptive stimuli and non-nociceptive, salient stimuli (such as low-probability sounds), leading to the proposal that nociception and salience share a common neural substrate in the human brain. Here we use high-resolution intracranial recordings from 13 neurosurgical patients (2,018 total electrodes) to show that neural representations of nociception and salience are anatomically and functionally distinct in the human brain. 77% of 107 electrodes that encoded nociceptive stimuli did not encode low-probability sounds ("nociceptive representations"), whereas 23% encoded both nociceptive and low-probability sounds ("salience representations"). Nociceptive representations were distinct from salience representations in terms of anatomical prevalence (posterior insula, inferior parietal, and perirolandic cortex vs. anterior insula, thalamus, and inferior frontal gyrus), timing (nociception preceded salience by 120 ms on a trial-by-trial basis), and function (intracranial electrical stimulation was more likely to cause sensory experience when applied near nociceptive representations, as compared to salience representations). These results provide strong evidence that nociception and salience have distinct neural substrates in the human brain, and that selective measurement of these distinct processes may help understand patient-to-patient variability in chronic pain and develop personalized brain stimulation treatments.

raw_data.title: Biophysical modeling of excitation/inhibition imbalance in Alzheimer's disease
raw_data.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's disease (AD) involves early sensory and perceptual changes that can precede memory decline. We developed a two-layer rate-based neural model of early and higher visual areas with feedforward, feedback, and recurrent connections to examine how excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance shapes visual motion perception in AD. METHODS: Using Motion-Induced Position Shift and Altered Motion Repulsion stimuli, we factorially manipulated excitatory (E) and inhibitory (I) subfield power and connectivity to examine their effects on illusion representation across visual layers. RESULTS: Increased E, decreased I, and increased E/I reduced illusion representation, consistent with reduced illusion susceptibility in AD, whereas the converse increased illusion representation, reflecting neurotypical processing. Higher-level layer 2 representations were more resistant to E/I perturbations than lower-level layer 1. Illusion representation was less affected by E/I increases in intra-areal (recurrent) connectivity than in inter-areal (feedforward/feedback) connectivity. DISCUSSION: This mechanistic framework links E/I balance and connectivity to altered visual motion illusion representations in AD and suggests that E/I and connectivity measures may provide probes of early AD neurobiology. The framework may also generalize beyond vision.

raw_data.title: Hippocampal extracellular matrix remodeling and temporally distinct glial reorganization following peripheral injury
raw_data.abstract: Chronic pain is frequently accompanied by anxiety and other affective disturbances, but the molecular and cellular changes linking peripheral injury to persistent alterations in brain function remain incompletely defined. The hippocampal extracellular matrix (ECM) regulates synaptic plasticity, cellular signaling, and neuroimmune interactions and may therefore contribute to pain-related central plasticity. We used a tibial fracture/cast immobilization model to examine temporal changes in hippocampal ECM, glial morphology, and affective behavior following peripheral injury. Behavioral testing was performed at 3, 7, and 20 weeks after injury, while high-dimensional morphometric analysis of microglia and astrocytes was performed at 1, 3, 7, and 20 weeks. Hippocampal ECM associated molecular signals were mapped at the chronic stage using decellularization coupled with MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry imaging. Injured mice developed mechanical hypersensitivity and reduced exploration in two anxiety related paradigms during the early and chronic stages, with these behavioral phenotypes no longer detected at 20 weeks. At 7 weeks, injury was associated with changes in hippocampal ECM-associated peptide signals, including reduced signals corresponding to four ECM-associated proteins. Microglia and astrocytes exhibited distinct, time-dependent changes in density and multidimensional morphology, with some alterations persisting after behavioral measures returned toward control levels. In vitro, BV2 microglia exhibited rigidity-dependent changes in morphology, phagocytic behavior, and calcium signaling. Together, these findings define a temporally evolving hippocampal ECM and glial phenotype following peripheral injury and identify matrix biomechanics as a candidate regulator of microglial function.

raw_data.title: Disease stage-sensitive MFSD2A-caveolae axis insigates hippocampal blood-brain barrier disruption in Alzheimer's disease
raw_data.abstract: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) malfunction contributes to pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the mechanisms that confer hippocampal endotheliocytes vulnerability remain unclear. Here we identify loss of endothelial major facilitator superfamily domain-containing protein 2A (MFSD2A), a suppressor of caveolae-mediated transcytosis, as an early and hippocampus-specific feature of AD-associated vascular impairment. In post-mortem human AD brains, reduction in hippocampal MFSD2A was accompanied with increased levels of caveolin-1 and perivascular albumin extravasation. Analysis of human single-nucleus transcriptomic data further demonstrated that vascular expression of MFSD2A declined during transition from mild cognitive impairment to established AD. In APP/PS1 mice, MFSD2A loss occurred early in hippocampal microvessels and coincided with disproportionately high hippocampal BBB leakage and reductions in GLUT1 and claudin-5, despite broader amyloid deposition throughout other brain regions. Restoration of endothelial MFSD2A using an AAV-BR1-based vascular vector during early stage of amyloid pathology, reduced albumin extravasation and preserved GLUT1 and claudin-5. Early intervention also reduced amyloid plaque burden and plaque-associated neuritic dystrophy, whereas this treatment during established amyloid pathology, although modifying selected endothelial markers, failed to reverse BBB leakage, amyloid pathology, or cognitive impairment. Sustained MFSD2A restoration from the early disease stage provided the greatest protection, preserving hippocampal BBB integrity, reducing amyloid and neuritic pathology, improving long-term potentiation and ameliorating spatial learning and memory deficits. These findings define endothelial MFSD2A loss as a disease stage-sensitive mechanism of hippocampal BBB vulnerability and highlight the MFSD2A-caveolae axis as a therapeutic target for early-stage AD.

raw_data.title: Accurate Hippocampal Electric Field Modeling for Electroconvulsive Therapy: Numerical Accuracy and Convergence
raw_data.abstract: Accurate hippocampal electric field (E-field) prediction is important for individualized electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) dosing and emerging deep-brain stimulation approaches such as temporal interference. Because hippocampal fields are far weaker than those beneath the stimulation electrodes, they are highly sensitive to tissue interfaces, conductivity contrasts, and numerical discretization, so numerical error can rival the physical uncertainties of anatomy and conductivity. We investigate this numerical component of hippocampal dosimetry using individualized head models from eleven ECT patients. Identical head40 segmentations, comprising 40 tissue compartments including the bilateral hippocampi, were simulated with three independent numerical methods: a charge-based boundary-element fast multipole method (BEM-FMM), a voxel-based hexahedral finite-element solver, and a conformal tetrahedral finite-element solver. For each, resolution was increased systematically and convergence assessed from the average hippocampal E-field magnitude. At the highest attainable resolutions, the three methods agreed closely, differing by 6%-7% in the left hippocampus and 9%-12% in the right. At default or coarse resolutions, however, they disagreed by 28.8% on average and up to 50.3% in the right hippocampus. Numerical convergence should therefore be established before differences are attributed to anatomical or conductivity uncertainty, and independent-solver agreement provides a practical basis for reliable hippocampal dosimetry.

raw_data.title: Longitudinal Impacts of Sex-Steroid Hormones on Cerebellar Structure in Adulthood are Sex Differentiated
raw_data.abstract: Sex-steroid hormones influence brain structure across aging, but their relationship to the cerebellum, a region implicated in cognition and vulnerable to age-related decline, remains poorly characterized, particularly longitudinally and across both sexes. We examined whether 17{beta}-estradiol, progesterone, and testosterone relate to cerebellar volume across two timepoints, and whether these relationships differ by sex. In a mixed-sex sample of aging adults (Baseline N = 137; Year 1 N = 93), free salivary hormones and cerebellar lobular volumes were quantified. Linear regression tested cross-sectional, predictive, and change-score hormone-volume associations, and formal hormone-by-sex interactions, in a priori primary and secondary cerebellar lobules of interest. Hormone-cerebellum relationships were consistently sex-differentiated. Estradiol change related to Crus I volume change in opposite directions in males and females, a dissociation extending across bilateral Crus I and Lobule VI, and Right Crus II. In females, greater increases in testosterone were associated with greater decline in Left Crus I and Right Lobule V volumes. In males, testosterone showed no significant associations in primary analyses, however, increases in estradiol were associated with larger volumes. Progesterone showed a male-specific cross-sectional association with Crus II. Several relationships ran opposite to the direction predicted by estradiols established neurotrophic role. Sex-steroid influences on the aging cerebellum are sex-differentiated, regionally specific, and may not be predicted exclusively by cortical or female-focused models. These findings establish the cerebellum as a potential site of sex-specific hormonal influence on brain aging and also further highlight the complexity of the impact of sex-steroid hormones on the aging brain.

raw_data.title: Impaired value estimation over space explains turn-induced freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease: A cortico-basal ganglia-inspired reinforcement learning model
raw_data.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) gait is characterized by reduced walking speed, short shuffling steps, increased double stance time, and increased step time variability. The most debilitating symptom in PD is freezing of gait (FOG), a context-dependent locomotion arrest, mostly occurring while encountering turns, obstacles, and narrow pathways. FOG is more pronounced during turning, a complex task that challenges motor planning and execution. Here, we simulate this phenomenon using a computational model inspired by the cortico-basal ganglia circuitry, based on reinforcement learning (RL) principles. In the model, the agent was trained to learn a value profile while navigating a path that involved turning. To simulate PD conditions, we clamped the temporal difference (TD) error, typically associated with dopaminergic signaling. Our model results show that compared to healthy controls (HC), PD non-freezers and PD freezers exhibit a reduction in turning velocity and step length, alongside an attenuated compensatory step-width widening at the sharpest turn, more pronounced in PD freezers, who additionally show increased step time variability. These kinematic impairments worsen during tighter turns. Ultimately, this model implicates FOG as a problem of impaired estimation of value over space and could potentially represent a generalized deficit in gait impairments in PD.

raw_data.title: Phase-targeted Poisson closed-loop peripheral nerve stimulation modulates sensorimotor oscillations in human MEG
raw_data.abstract: Closed-loop brain stimulation offers a promising approach for modulating neural oscillations, but the mechanisms of phase-dependent neuromodulation remain poorly understood. We developed a real-time MEG-based closed-loop system delivering median nerve stimulation using a phase-modulated Poisson process. Sixteen healthy participants (11 female, 5 male) underwent open-loop characterization followed by closed-loop testing of eight phase-offset conditions (0 degrees-315 degrees), each paired with a statistically matched replay control. Closed-loop stimulation induced robust phase-dependent modulation (14.21 +/- 8.24%) versus replay (7.03 +/- 2.95%; p = 0.0003), with consistent phase specificity across participants (circular mean: 70.2 degrees, referenced to each individual's dominant frequency). At the group level, alpha oscillations (8-12 Hz) showed bidirectional modulation (mean boost: +21.0 +/- 19.9% at 0 degrees-135 degrees; mean suppression: -13.3 +/- 10.8% at 180 degrees-315 degrees), while beta oscillations (13-30 Hz) showed predominantly unidirectional suppression (-9.3 +/- 9.6%). Successful fixed-frequency targeting required alignment with each individual's natural peak. Misalignment led to different phase shifts producing power at different frequencies, a phenomenon we term phase-frequency coupling. Dynamic frequency tracking (8-30 Hz) automatically identified and targeted each individual's natural peak, achieving robust bidirectional modulation without prior knowledge of peak location. These findings demonstrate that real-time phase-locked peripheral nerve stimulation selectively modulates sensorimotor oscillations beyond statistically matched open-loop stimulation. The distinct phase-excitability relationships of alpha and beta oscillations, together with the importance of aligning stimulation with individual natural peaks, establish principled guidelines for personalized closed-loop neuromodulation.

raw_data.title: Connectomics by Sequencing Reveals Self-Organizing Principles of Neuronal Networks in Cerebral Organoids
raw_data.abstract:
Functional neural networks emerge as developing neurons form synaptic connections. Revealing how these connections are organized and perturbed in disease requires linking single-neuron connectivity to molecular state across thousands of networks, which is challenging with current methods. We developed COSCO (Connectomics by Sequencing in Cerebral Organoids), combining barcoded monosynaptic rabies tracing with single-cell RNA sequencing to reconstruct over 10,000 networks across organoids. We demonstrate that organoid circuitry self-organizes into stereotyped network motifs governed by cell-intrinsic wiring rules aligning with features of mouse cortical connectivity. Projecting network topology onto transcriptomic space reveals that wiring correlates with cell-adhesion and synaptic gene expression programs. In a Tuberous Sclerosis Complex model, pathological hyperexcitability coincides with topological rewiring: mutant networks become more heterogeneous, driven by the transcriptional distribution of upper layer excitatory cell states. This work establishes cerebral organoids as a model to study self-organization of human connectivity, and its disruption in neurodevelopmental disease.

paper.title: Connectomics by Sequencing Reveals Self-Organizing Principles of Neuronal Networks in Cerebral Organoids
paper.abstract:
Functional neural networks emerge as developing neurons form synaptic connections. Revealing how these connections are organized and perturbed in disease requires linking single-neuron connectivity to molecular state across thousands of networks, which is challenging with current methods. We developed COSCO (Connectomics by Sequencing in Cerebral Organoids), combining barcoded monosynaptic rabies tracing with single-cell RNA sequencing to reconstruct over 10,000 networks across organoids. We demonstrate that organoid circuitry self-organizes into stereotyped network motifs governed by cell-intrinsic wiring rules aligning with features of mouse cortical connectivity. Projecting network topology onto transcriptomic space reveals that wiring correlates with cell-adhesion and synaptic gene expression programs. In a Tuberous Sclerosis Complex model, pathological hyperexcitability coincides with topological rewiring: mutant networks become more heterogeneous, driven by the transcriptional distribution of upper layer excitatory cell states. This work establishes cerebral organoids as a model to study self-organization of human connectivity, and its disruption in neurodevelopmental disease.

title_zh: 通过测序进行连接组学揭示脑类器官中神经网络的自组织原理
recommendation_text: 该研究开发了COSCO技术，将条形码化单突触狂犬病毒示踪与单细胞RNA测序结合，首次在类脑器官中重建了超过10,000个单神经元连接网络。这项工作揭示了类脑器官神经网络自组织形成刻板网络模体的原则，并将单细胞连接性与分子状态直接关联。对于神经科学领域，COSCO为研究人类神经元网络发育、疾病相关连接异常提供了高通量、分子分辨的新范式，有望推动发育神经生物学和神经疾病建模的进展。
reasoning: 该研究开发了COSCO技术，将单神经元连接与转录组关联，属于神经科学方法学核心创新，直接推动连接组学和脑类器官研究。
feature_angle: 利用条形码单突触狂犬病毒追踪与单细胞RNA测序相结合，首次在人类脑类器官中重建超过1万个神经元网络，揭示连接的自组织规则及其在疾病中的重塑。
key_strength: 开发了COSCO技术，将单神经元连接性与转录组状态联系起来，并在结节性硬化症模型中揭示了网络拓扑重塑与病理过度兴奋的关联。
key_limitation: 仍为bioRxiv预印本，尚未经过同行评审；类器官模型缺乏体内完整环境，且狂犬病毒追踪可能存在效率偏差，结论的普适性需进一步验证。
target_audience: 神经科学、发育生物学、计算生物学、疾病建模及连接组学研究领域的科研人员。
editor_note: 方法学创新显著，结合病毒示踪与单细胞测序，适用于类器官和发育研究。

raw_data.title: Objective markers of altered neural gain dissociate tinnitus and self-reported listening problems in individuals with exceptional hearing thresholds
raw_data.abstract: Many individuals experience problems that are undetected by standard hearing tests, such as persistent tinnitus and difficulties understanding speech in background noise. Here, we report evidence of altered neural gain in young adults with self-reported listening problems despite exceptional hearing thresholds. Individuals reporting persistent tinnitus (the daily percept of sound in the absence of an external source) exhibited elevated thresholds of the middle ear muscle reflex, suggestive of altered gain in brainstem reflexive circuits, and reduced cortical responses to auditory spatial cues conveyed in the temporal fine structure of low-frequency sounds. Moreover, in both groups, greater self-reported speech-in-noise difficulties were associated with higher magnitude cortical responses, particularly at the highest stimulus intensity, consistent with elevated neural gain. Using a conceptual model, we demonstrate how damage to high-threshold auditory nerve fibres innervating cochlear nuclei can account for reduced activity of binaural neurons sensitive to the temporal fine structure of low-frequency sounds, generating a compensatory increase in neural gain in higher brain centres that impacts listening in complex environments.

raw_data.title: cyto7: an open, vertex-level cortical type atlas of the human cortex
raw_data.abstract: The cerebral cortex is organized along a gradient of laminar complexity, indexed principally by the emergence and granularity of layer IV and by the size of layer III neuron somata, and cortical types are the ordered categories along it. The Structural Model builds on that gradient to predict laminar connectivity, plasticity and disease vulnerability (Barbas and Rempel-Clower, 1997; Garcia-Cabezas et al., 2019). Existing digital cortical-type maps are area-level: they assign one type per classical area and cannot represent a type boundary that runs through an area. We release cyto7, an open, vertex-level, seven-type cortical-type atlas delineated on the fsaverage surface following the Garcia-Cabezas protocol and revised by the protocol's authors. We distribute the atlas with a reusable quality-control and support framework. A topological audit reports the map against four spatial rules that follow from cortical type analysis and the dual origin of the neocortex theory: neighbouring vertices differ by at most one type, the least complex cortex forms one continuous limbic belt, eulaminate II forms a single matrix enclosing a few holes, and eulaminate III and koniocortex form isolated islands. These were imposed during construction rather than tested, and the audit reports what imposing them cost. A vertex-wise benchmark against the existing area-level map, one type per von Economo-Koskinas area, shows exact agreement at 52.5% of vertices, with disagreement almost always a single level and concentrated inside the large, heterogeneous areas that a single areal label cannot resolve. Where the two maps disagree, cyto7's label better matches the independent multimodal profile in 60.1% of pooled feature-by-vertex comparisons, against 46% under a rotation null and 54% under granularity-matched alternative partitions (p = 0.020), the harder of the two. A per-vertex anatomical support score, computed from anatomy alone, states how strongly each hand-drawn label is backed by the anatomical evidence, and is deliberately not a calibrated error probability. We then validate cyto7 against independent brain measures not used to define it, under a spatial-autocorrelation (spin) null with FDR control. Intracortical myelin (T1w/T2w) increases, cortical thickness decreases, and the principal functional-connectivity gradient reverses along the type axis (all q of about 0.006 or less). Source-reconstructed resting-state MEG dynamics also track the axis: the intrinsic timescale shortens toward koniocortex (rho of about -0.46) and survives the null, as do the spectral centroid and the slow/fast band-power ratio, whereas the aperiodic 1/f exponent does not. The laminar marker genes are where cyto7 differs most from a quantisation of a continuous map: it shows a larger absolute correlation with the layer-IV marker RORB (rho = +0.78) and the layer-V marker FEZF2 (-0.59) than seven-level septiles of myelin, of the functional gradient or of a histological gradient, on four of five markers, while tying or losing to those septiles on the macroscale proxies. These are larger observed associations against three tested quantisations, not a test that the differences between maps are reliable, and they do not establish the accuracy of any individual boundary. Defined from anatomy alone, cyto7 recovers the sensorimotor-to-association hierarchy and, on these markers, some of the laminar signal underlying it. It is released with its full pipeline and an uncalibrated anatomical support score as a reusable substrate for structure-function and modelling studies.

raw_data.title: A dynamical attractor computes reward prediction in the basal forebrain
raw_data.abstract: Phasic ensemble bursting in subcortical neuromodulatory systems such as the basal forebrain (BF) provides a powerful format for broadcasting reward-prediction signals. These bursts encode reward prediction by varying population amplitude, yet their internal structure, reflected in cell-to-cell amplitude relationships, remains conserved. How neural circuits reconcile these competing constraints remains unknown. Here we show that BF bursting is generated by a dynamical attractor: burst structure is imposed not by feedforward inputs but by recurrent circuit dynamics, while burst amplitude is determined by approximately linear integration across concurrent inputs. Optogenetic activation of BF neurons expressing natriuretic peptide receptor 3 (Npr3) outside the behavioral task reproduced the low-dimensional dynamics of natural cue-evoked bursting, preserving the temporal envelope and cell-to-cell amplitude relationships across stimulation patterns. Critically, unilateral activation of non-overlapping Npr3 populations in either hemisphere recruited the full bilateral ensemble into the same native trajectory, showing that restricted inputs can nevertheless recruit the full ensemble. Matched ipsilateral and contralateral onset latencies exceeding 25 ms implicated recurrent interactions beyond the BF. Despite the conserved structure, population burst amplitude varied with stimulation strength and summed approximately linearly across concurrent unilateral inputs. This linear summation extended to natural sensory input during behavior: adding Npr3 stimulation to auditory cues increased cue-evoked burst amplitude, improved detection, and reduced subsequent reward responses, consistent with stronger reward prediction producing smaller reward prediction errors. Thus, a low-dimensional dynamical attractor preserves a shared BF burst structure across diverse inputs while integrating concurrent inputs into a scalar burst amplitude that encodes reward prediction.

title_zh: 基底前脑中的动态吸引子计算奖赏预测
recommendation_text: 该研究揭示基底前脑的群体爆发放电由一个动态吸引子产生：爆发结构由局部递归回路动力学而非前馈输入决定，而爆发幅度则取决于外部输入或网络状态。这解决了神经调控系统如何同时满足“结构保守”与“幅度灵活编码奖励预测”这一矛盾，为理解强化学习信号广播的环路机制提供了新的理论框架，并提示吸引子动力学可能是多种神经调控系统（如多巴胺、去甲肾上腺素）的通用计算基元。
reasoning: 该研究直接解析基底前脑神经环路如何通过动态吸引子生成奖赏预测信号，属于系统与环路神经科学的核心问题。
feature_angle: 基底前脑爆发由低维动力吸引子生成：结构由循环动力学决定，幅度线性整合多路输入并编码奖励预测。
key_strength: 结合光遗传学、双侧独立激活、行为任务和动力学建模，将Npr3群体活动与奖励预测误差直接联系起来，概念新颖。
key_limitation: 机制推论主要依赖光遗传扰动和相关性分析，缺乏直接因果干预和细胞类型特异性操作；预印本未经同行评审，公式化模型细节未充分提供。
target_audience: 系统神经科学、计算神经科学、神经调控与强化学习研究者
editor_note: 适合作为系统神经科学与计算神经科学交叉的理论机制亮点，强调吸引子动力学在神经调控中的普适性。

raw_data.title: Individualized Gabor Flicker for Well-Tolerated Neural Entrainment During Working Memory
raw_data.abstract: Rhythmic visual stimulation offers a non-invasive means of modulating oscillatory brain activity, but conventional flicker may induce considerable visual discomfort. We developed an individualized Gabor flicker stimulation designed to balance neural entrainment and tolerability. In Experiment 1, thirty-four participants passively viewed Plain and Gabor flickers presented at their individual alpha frequency (IAF), IAF - 2 Hz, or IAF + 2 Hz, and at threshold-adjusted or full intensity. Steady-state visual evoked potential signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) was highest at IAF and increased with intensity. Plain and Gabor flickers produced comparable overall SNR, but Gabor flicker was rated as substantially more comfortable and less mentally fatiguing, with stimulation at IAF providing the most favorable balance between neural entrainment and tolerability. In Experiment 2, the optimized stimulation parameters were applied during a retro-cue working memory task using individualized theta and alpha frequency flickers. Stimulation increased SNR and inter-trial phase coherence relative to a non rhythmic Natural condition. No behavioral benefit was observed in the full sample. However, an exploratory subgroup analysis indicated higher accuracy with theta stimulation of cued representations and alpha stimulation of uncued representations than in the Natural condition among participants who showed limited baseline retro-cue benefits. These findings show that individualized Gabor flicker can provide robust and well-tolerated neural entrainment during passive viewing and working memory retention, although its behavioral effects may vary across individuals according to their cognitive performance.

raw_data.title: Transient Vascular Cell Integration and Intrinsic Media-Stimulated Endothelial Activation Reveal Diabetic Retinopathy Signatures in Human Retinal Organoids
raw_data.abstract: Retinal organoids (ROs) model human retinogenesis but remain avascular and lack immune components, limiting their utility for studying vascular retinopathies. We generated vascular organoids (VOrs) from human pluripotent stem cells and evaluated their integration into developing ROs. Dissociated VOr cells (day 12 or day 30) were seeded onto 2D retinal neuroepithelium before 3D transition, followed by long-term culture to day 210. VOr derived cells migrated into ROs and transiently persisted. V30 ROs preserved retinal lamination, major neuronal subtypes and light evoked retinal ganglion cell responses comparable to non vascularised controls, whereas media-only ROs cultured in proangiogenic conditions showed structural disorganisation and reduced neuronal survival. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed an endogenous, inflammatory endothelial-like population with partial endothelial-to-mesenchymal features and a perivascular fibroblast-like cluster in pro-angiogenic media only RO controls. The endothelial-like cell cluster was significantly enriched for genes upregulated in human retinal endothelial cells exposed to high glucose, indicating a diabetic retinopathy like transcriptional state. Microglia like and border associated macrophage populations were present across all conditions, with developmental shifts in morphology and marker expression. Our findings define conditions under which vascular cells can be incorporated into human ROs without disrupting retinal architecture, while uncovering an intrinsic capacity for inflammatory endothelial activation that partially recapitulates diabetic retinopathy. This work advances the engineering of vascularised, immunocompetent retinal models and highlights endogenous vascular immune programmes that must be considered when modelling retinal disease in vitro.

paper.title: Transient Vascular Cell Integration and Intrinsic Media-Stimulated Endothelial Activation Reveal Diabetic Retinopathy Signatures in Human Retinal Organoids
paper.abstract: Retinal organoids (ROs) model human retinogenesis but remain avascular and lack immune components, limiting their utility for studying vascular retinopathies. We generated vascular organoids (VOrs) from human pluripotent stem cells and evaluated their integration into developing ROs. Dissociated VOr cells (day 12 or day 30) were seeded onto 2D retinal neuroepithelium before 3D transition, followed by long-term culture to day 210. VOr derived cells migrated into ROs and transiently persisted. V30 ROs preserved retinal lamination, major neuronal subtypes and light evoked retinal ganglion cell responses comparable to non vascularised controls, whereas media-only ROs cultured in proangiogenic conditions showed structural disorganisation and reduced neuronal survival. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed an endogenous, inflammatory endothelial-like population with partial endothelial-to-mesenchymal features and a perivascular fibroblast-like cluster in pro-angiogenic media only RO controls. The endothelial-like cell cluster was significantly enriched for genes upregulated in human retinal endothelial cells exposed to high glucose, indicating a diabetic retinopathy like transcriptional state. Microglia like and border associated macrophage populations were present across all conditions, with developmental shifts in morphology and marker expression. Our findings define conditions under which vascular cells can be incorporated into human ROs without disrupting retinal architecture, while uncovering an intrinsic capacity for inflammatory endothelial activation that partially recapitulates diabetic retinopathy. This work advances the engineering of vascularised, immunocompetent retinal models and highlights endogenous vascular immune programmes that must be considered when modelling retinal disease in vitro.

raw_data.title: Design and Test Novel EEG Electrode Attachments for Type 4 Afro-textured Hairstyles
raw_data.abstract: Black participants remain underrepresented in electroencephalography (EEG) research, partly because current EEG devices work poorly with dense, coily Type 4 Afro-textured hair. Research-grade EEG typically wires electrodes on a cap, and therefore the electrodes often fail to reach the scalp through dense, Afro-textured hair. Protocols that ask Black participants to unbraid or restyle protective hairstyles add burdens that discourage enrollment in research studies. To address this, we designed and tested 3D-printed attachments that fit onto an EEG electrode and anchored it directly in the hair, using the hairstyle itself as the mounting structure. We fabricated three design configurations for natural Afro-textured hair, cornrows/braids, and twists/microlocs. Seventeen healthy adults with Type 4a-4c hair used electrode attachments that matched their hairstyle. During a single visit, EEG was recorded with 16 conventional cap electrodes defined by the international 10-20 system and with 16 electrodes using novel electrode attachments anchored directly to their hair. Participants completed resting and walking trials with each system. Electrode-to-scalp distance and gel volume were measured during setup. Electrode disconnection, impedance, signal quality (i.e. peak alpha power and aperiodic (1/f) component), and comfort level were measured throughout the data collection. Compared with the conventional cap, the novel attachments reduced electrode-to-scalp distance, gel use, and impedance. Twenty percent of the conventional cap electrodes failed to connect to the scalp compared with 0.1% of novel electrodes. Impedance rose across trials for the conventional cap, whereas the novel attachments showed a smaller increase and maintained lower impedance throughout. Signal quality was significantly better using the novel attachments, while comfort level did not differ between systems. In conclusion, hair-anchored electrode attachment may present a feasible alternative to conventional cap-based EEG for people with Type 4 hair, yielding more usable channels and better signal quality, and supporting more inclusive EEG acquisition.

raw_data.title: Distilling Trial-Level EEG Variability into Participant Representations: Neurophysiologically Constrained Graph Learning in ADHD
raw_data.abstract: Extracting stable individual-level representations from noisy and variable trial-wise EEG remains a major challenge in computational cognitive neuroscience. We developed a spatiotemporal graph attention network to analyze Go/NoGo EEG from children and adolescents with and without ADHD. The framework combines ERP-informed temporal windows, phase-synchrony graph priors, and trial-to-participant transfer learning, making both information routing and representation geometry explicitly testable. The model learned reproducible attention trajectories, yet ADHD and control participants did not differ reliably in spatial attention allocation. Instead, group-related structure emerged in compact participant-level embeddings that distilled trial-level variability and retained discriminative information beyond convolutional representations. Performance exceeded a convolutional neural network comparison, but the central advance is methodological: neurophysiologically constrained graph learning can reveal where diagnostically relevant information emerges within the analytical pipeline. This provides a framework for developing auditable cognitive-neurophysiological markers of neurodevelopmental variation.

raw_data.title: Glia-enriched human brain organoids for studying developmental alterations in leukodystrophies
raw_data.abstract: Leukodystrophies (LKD) comprise mostly inherited white matter disorders whose developmental origins and underlying pathomechanisms remain poorly understood. Progress has been limited by restricted access to human primary tissue and by the inability of animal models to fully recapitulate human neurodevelopment. Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neural organoids provide an alternative approach, but most culture systems do not capture later, glia-rich developmental stages relevant to these diseases. Recent studies have shown that appropriate patterning cues and long in vitro differentiation can generate neuroglial spheroids comprising multiple neuronal and macroglial populations, including mature oligodendrocytes. Here, we adapt the human oligodendrocyte (hOLS) spheroid platform to establish 3D models of globoid cell leukodystrophy (GLD), 4H leukodystrophy (4H), and Canavan disease (CD). Here we adapt this organoid platform to establish 3D models of globoid cell leukodystrophy (GLD), 4H leukodystrophy (4H), and Canavan disease (CD). Across 150 days of differentiation, hOLS from different genetic backgrounds displayed largely comparable growth kinetics and developmental trajectories, comprising multiple neuroglial cell types with predominantly ventral forebrain and midbrain identities. Comparison of LKD and control hOLS revealed both shared and disease-specific alterations, with prominent transcriptional changes in lysosomal, metabolic, and stress-response pathways. Lineage-resolved pathway analysis further identified signatures across individual LKDs, including mitochondrial and translational stress in GLD glial lineages, disruption of RNA metabolic and cell-cycle pathways in 4H, and prominent astrocyte-centered metabolic dysregulation in CD. Our results establish hOLS as a human 3D in vitro platform for studying the impact of LKD-associated genetic variants on early neural development and for dissecting lineage-specific disease vulnerability.

raw_data.title: Psychedelics restructure information in the human brain
raw_data.abstract: How do psychedelic drugs alter human brain function? Answering this question relies on our ability to understand how information is stored, transferred, and transformed across the cortex. Here, we leverage a precise mathematical framework for multivariate information decomposition to construct the first comprehensive picture of these processes across five compounds: LSD, psilocybin, ketamine, DMT and 5-MeO-DMT (N=80). We provide a formal and empirical explanation of major prior results, revealing sets of competing underlying phenomena masked by extant approaches. We extend this analysis to novel higher-order phenomena, and we demonstrate how all of these observations can emerge from a minimal generative model in which neural populations operate with reduced self-coupling. In sum, our results suggest that the psychedelic brain is one in which cortical populations become alike, but not necessarily together. This has important implications for models of how psychedelics reorganize brain dynamics to alter subjective experience and alleviate mental health conditions.

raw_data.title: "Spilling-in" versus "Filling-in": Disentangling bottom-up drive from predictive completion in human V1 to V3
raw_data.abstract: It is well established that responses in visual areas are a combination of bottom-up stimulus driven input and top-down input driven by expectation. However, it has been difficult to quantify the differential strength of these components, and how they vary across the visual hierarchy. Here, we introduce a method for dissociating bottom-up and top-down contributions in early retinotopic areas (V1-V3). Using a log-scaled bar stimulus, we measured BOLD responses under full-field vs. central scotoma conditions. Using the full-field stimulus, we estimated pRFs in human visual cortex 17 (V1-V3).

raw_data.title: Preconceptional social isolation alters inflammatory and transcriptional signalling across the placenta-fetal brain axis
raw_data.abstract: Maternal depression and psychosocial adversity during pregnancy are associated with altered offspring neurodevelopment, yet the molecular processes linking maternal state to the developing fetus remain incompletely understood. The placenta is positioned to sense and respond to maternal physiological signals, but how placental molecular responses relate to those in the developing brain is unclear. Here, we used a mouse model of prolonged social isolation initiated before conception and maintained throughout pregnancy to investigate inflammatory and transcriptional alterations across matched placenta and fetal-brain samples at gestational day 18. Maternal social isolation altered cytokine profiles in both tissues and induced extensive transcriptional changes in the placenta, with a more restricted response in the fetal brain. Functional analyses identified alterations in placental immune, metabolic and transport-related programmes and fetal-brain immune, neuronal and proliferative processes. Although sex-stratified analyses revealed different transcriptional profiles in male and female tissues, formal maternal housing x fetal-sex interaction testing did not identify significant gene-level interaction effects. Cross-tissue co-expression analysis initially identified extensive covariation between social-isolation-responsive placental and fetal-brain modules; however, most associations were attenuated after accounting for their shared relationship with maternal housing. An exposure-independent network analysis nevertheless identified an inverse pregnancy-level association between a placental module enriched for immune and interferon-related signalling and a fetal-brain module enriched for cell-cycle and proliferative processes. Together, these findings show that prolonged maternal social adversity is associated with coordinated but tissue-distinct molecular alterations across the placenta-fetal brain axis and demonstrate the importance of distinguishing parallel responses to a common maternal environment from direct cross-tissue molecular coupling.

Here, we used a mouse model of prolonged social isolation initiated before conception and maintained throughout pregnancy to investigate inflammatory and transcriptional alterations across matched placenta and fetal-brain samples at gestational day 18. Maternal social isolation altered cytokine profiles in both tissues and induced extensive transcriptional changes in the placenta, with a more restricted response in the fetal brain. Functional analyses identified alterations in placental immune, metabolic and transport-related programmes and fetal-brain immune, neuronal and proliferative processes. Although sex-stratified analyses revealed different transcriptional profiles in male and female tissues, formal maternal housing x fetal-sex interaction testing did not identify significant gene-level interaction effects. Cross-tissue co-expression analysis initially identified extensive covariation between social-isolation-responsive placental and fetal-brain modules; however, most associations were attenuated after accounting for their shared relationship with maternal housing. An exposure-independent network analysis nevertheless identified an inverse pregnancy-level association between a placental module enriched for immune and interferon-related signalling and a fetal-brain module enriched for cell-cycle and proliferative processes. Together, these findings show that prolonged maternal social adversity is associated with coordinated but tissue-distinct molecular alterations across the placenta-fetal brain axis and demonstrate the importance of distinguishing parallel responses to a common maternal environment from direct cross-tissue molecular coupling.

raw_data.title: Volitional control of a recurrent brain computer interface via covert reinforcement of endogenous reward networks
raw_data.abstract: Recurrent brain-computer interfaces (rBCIs) deliver targeted stimulation to one brain region based on neural activity recorded and processed in real-time at another. In a volitionally controlled rBCI, the user must also learn to intentionally produce the triggering neural activity, a process typically facilitated by an external reward. However, reliance on an external reward introduces a delay between the triggering event and reinforcement that can slow association between the two and, ultimately, control of the rBCI (particularly for neural activity not directly related to an observable behavior such as a goal-directed movement). The constraint to an external reward also limits studies of neural dynamics during natural, free behavior. In contrast, delivering activity-dependent stimulation directly to the brain's own reward centers - i.e., covert reinforcement - would bypass the need for external feedback, enabling precise temporal coupling between triggering events and reward and allowing for unrestrained rBCI use. Here, we show that rats can gain volitional control of an rBCI using activity-dependent electrical stimulation of the medial forebrain bundle as a sole reinforcer. Animals successfully learned to modulate motor unit discharge rates as well as specific electrocorticographic frequency bands (beta and gamma) to self-trigger stimulation. Furthermore, rats demonstrated flexible control by independently modulating distinct spectral features from the same cortical site. These findings suggest that covert reinforcement of endogenous reward networks can drive operant conditioning of specific neural signals during unrestrained behavior, opening new avenues for adaptive BCIs and closed-loop psychiatric therapies.

raw_data.title: Distinct cortical networks associated with subregions of the hippocampal-entorhinal system in the first two years of human life
raw_data.abstract: Episodic memory critically depends on the hippocampus and the entorhinal cortex. Despite a rapid developmental change in human episodic memory during the first two years of life, little is known about the developmental trajectory of the hippocampal-entorhinal circuitry during this critical time period. In the current study, we collected high-quality precision fMRI data from five typically developing infants over the time period between 1 and 2 years of life and examined, in great anatomical detail, the developmental profile of distinct parts of the infant hippocampal-entorhinal system and their coupling with distinct cortical networks. We show that already at around 1 year of age, subdivisions of the canonical default network (DN) are fully dissociated at the neocortex and are differently associated with the hippocampal-entorhinal system, with tentatively differential developmental trajectories. While the DN-A, associated with episodic simulation, coupled with the anterior hippocampus and the medial part of the entorhinal cortex, the DN-B, associated with social cognition, showed significantly weaker connectivity with the hippocampal-entorhinal system. Furthermore, the parietal memory network coupled with the posterior hippocampus and the lateral part of the entorhinal cortex. Exploratory longitudinal results suggest that associations of the DN-B with the hippocampus and the entorhinal cortex increase towards the end of the second postnatal year, and the associations of the parietal memory network become more topographically restricted to the posterior hippocampus. These networks and their differential maturation may provide the basis for important developments in episodic memory and social cognition in the second postnatal year and suggest that potentially unique properties of human hippocampal-entorhinal circuitry may emerge latest in development.

raw_data.title: Neural circuit mechanisms for multi-tasking
raw_data.abstract: Neural activity during performance of a cognitive or motor task is often described as lying on a low-dimensional manifold in the space of all possible activity patterns. When multiple tasks are performed, an individual brain region's activity may generate multiple such manifolds. Several models have been introduced to explain this capability, each with different assumptions concerning architecture and inputs. Here, we develop a theory of multi-tasking according to which models and experimental paradigms can be organized. We introduce a distinction between sequential and simultaneous multi-tasking, the performance of one task at a time or multiple in parallel. We show that interference between tasks often prevents multi-tasking and introduce a model of ``task barcodes" that circumvents this problem and parameterizes a neuronal population's task selectivity. Our theory reveals categorical distinctions between neural circuit mechanisms supporting multi-tasking that can be probed using physiological recordings.

raw_data.title: Huntingtin and Celsr3 Orchestrate Spontaneous Long-Distance Spinal Cord Regeneration
raw_data.abstract: Spontaneous spinal cord regeneration is an endogenous process operational in diverse vertebrate and select mammalian species. Yet despite resulting in functional regeneration, axonal regrowth dynamics as well as underlying molecular programs are largely unknown. Live-cell imaging following laser axotomy of individual zebrafish spinal cord M-cell axons reveals a time-sensitive multistep process. From a genetic screen we uncover previously unrecognized roles for two evolutionary conserved genes, celsr3 and huntingtin (htt) in spontaneous spinal cord regeneration. Specifically, we find that htt is critical to initiate a transcriptional injury response in regenerating M-cells, enabling their axon to traverse the injury site. Once axons cross the injury site celsr3 functions to increase growth rates, while both celsr3 and htt function to sustain long-range axonal growth. Moreover, we show that htt is dispensable for optic nerve and peripheral motor neuron regeneration, and that reducing soma-to-injury site distance in htt mutant M-cell axons partially restores regeneration, demonstrating a selective role in long-range CNS axon regeneration. Consistent with a transport-based mechanism, genetic knockdown of htt-associated axonal transport proteins recapitulates the htt mutant regeneration phenotype. Combined, our results provide compelling evidence for a time and distance-sensitive multistep molecular framework in which celsr3 dependent growth rate modulation and htt dependent axonal transport promote spontaneous, long-range spinal cord regeneration.

raw_data.title: Brain-wide Cerebrospinal Fluid Recirculation Collapse in Alzheimers Disease
raw_data.abstract:
Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow and the glymphatic system are essential for maintaining brain homeostasis, yet the precise mechanisms driving their profound failure in Alzheimers disease (AD) remain largely elusive. Here, we reveal that macroscopic CSF propagates dorsally via the perivascular spaces (PAS) of major ventral arteries--the Circle of Willis (CW), middle cerebral artery (MCA), and olfactory artery (OlfA)--which undergo severe structural degradation in an AD mouse model. High-resolution imaging of the dorsal cortex demonstrates that this structural collapse induces a severe influx blockade; in AD, CSF tracers form massive aggregates within the PAS, physically decoupling the gliovascular interface, while tracers entering the parenchyma are pathologically sequestered by amyloid plaques. Furthermore, we identify an active, cholesterol-mediated clearance mechanism responding to exogenous CSF tracer infiltration. While healthy brains rapidly synthesize and efficiently clear this cholesterol via vascular efflux within 120 minutes, the AD model exhibits blunted cholesterol mobilization and a complete failure of capillary efflux. This terminal bottleneck forces uncleared cholesterol to retrogradely accumulate into pathological aggregates within perivascular pericytes and neuronal somata. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that AD dismantles the entire CSF recirculation loop--from macroscopic ventral entry to terminal microvascular efflux--highlighting pericytic and neuronal lipidosis as fundamental drivers of brain fluid stagnation.

raw_data.title: LLM-powered automatic scoring tools for memory recall
raw_data.abstract: Free recall of naturalistic stimuli, such as films and stories, reveals what people remember and how they organize it. Scoring such recall requires matching each recalled utterance to the encoded stimulus, and doing this manually often makes large studies impractical. Existing automated methods mostly return similarity or aggregate scores rather than explicit matches between recalled and stimulus content. Here we introduce an open-source, model-agnostic pipeline that uses a large language model (LLM) to divide the stimulus and the recall into information units and to match units between the two texts. The output is a table of unit-to-unit matches with accuracy labels, from which standard analysis scripts compute recall measures. We validated the pipeline with four LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT 5.4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Gemini 2.5 Flash) on three datasets. On typed recall of four short stories, agreement between each model and two trained raters ({phi} = .73-.79) was close to the agreement between the raters themselves ({phi} = .77). A second run reproduced each model's matches ({phi} = .91-.97) more closely than the raters agreed with each other. On spoken recall of 10 films, every model attributed recall to the correct film with high agreement. On uncorrected speech-to-text recall of a television episode, agreement varied more across models. The median cost was under $1 per participant for every model. These results suggest that the pipeline can serve as a reliable, low-cost alternative to manual scoring of free recall.

raw_data.title: Social feedback structures stay/switch decision-making in Drosophila
raw_data.abstract: Within natural environments, different sensory stimuli can drive mutually-exclusive behaviors such as fighting, feeding, or courting. When experiencing competing cues, how do animals decide to continue executing the current behavior or to switch to a new behavior? To address this question, we developed a closed-loop behavioral paradigm that presents actively courting male Drosophila with a fictive heat stimulus, forcing the male to choose between two competing behaviors: continue courting (stay) or escape the heat (switch). By modeling the sensorimotor transformations underlying this decision process, we discovered that male flies continually evaluate social cues, including female speed and her distance, in order to make a stay/switch decision. We investigated the neural correlates of stay/switch decision-making via brain-wide calcium imaging in head-fixed male flies presented with both fictive female visual cues and heat stimuli. We built models that predicted stay/switch decisions from neural data, which revealed that activity in a small number of brain regions, including the anterior optic tubercle, predicted decision outcomes up to 4 seconds prior to stimulus onset, whereas after stimulus onset, distributed activity across the brain was correlated with the behavioral decision. Together, these results demonstrate that Drosophila continually evaluate social feedback to inform decisions about how to respond to environmental cues, and that brain activity changes prior to presentation of the environmental cue can inform upcoming decisions. Overall, this study provides new insight into the processes underlying naturalistic decision-making in Drosophila.

raw_data.title: Path Integration Promotes Flexible Navigational Decision Making
raw_data.abstract: Flexible decision making depends on internal representations that capture the latent structure of a task, allowing prior knowledge to be applied in novel circumstances. Spatial navigation provides a useful model for studying flexible choice behavior, because spatial location is itself a latent variable that must be inferred rather than directly perceived. Here, we trained rats on a navigation task that required them to reach the same goal via two distinct paths from different starting locations, and then return to one of the two starting locations before beginning the next trial. Some rats were trained to rely on distal visual landmarks, allowing task states to be identified from current sensory information, whereas others were trained to rely on path integration, requiring task states to be inferred from self-motion information accumulated over the preceding trajectory. Rats trained to rely on path integration acquired the task similarly to rats trained to rely on distal visual landmarks. However, reliance on path integration enhanced rats' ability to generalize their learning to novel situations, including finding the goal from an untrained starting location and adapting to a relocated goal that reversed learned choice sequences. These findings suggest that reliance on path integration promotes the acquisition and use of mental representations that capture the latent spatial structure of navigational tasks, thereby favoring flexible navigational decisions over rigid retrieval of reinforced responses. More broadly, our findings demonstrate how information available during training can shape representations learned from experience and thereby constrain the flexibility of decision making during inference.

raw_data.title: Self-Exciting Population Event Models Reveal Abnormal Temporal Amplification in MAPT-Mutant Human Brain Assembloids
raw_data.abstract: Human brain assembloids provide a tractable platform for studying mutation-specific network dysfunction, but most studies do not distinguish whether abnormal activity arises from increased spontaneous initiation or stronger history-dependent amplification. We introduce a low-dimensional discrete-time self-exciting population model for calcium-imaging event sequences that separates baseline initiation (%[mu]), integrated history-dependent gain (%[eta]), and memory decay (%[tau]). Across 175 recordings from 13 MAPT p.R406W or CRISPR-corrected isogenic assembloids, biological-unit inference identified a 4.31-fold increase in %[eta] in mutants (95% CI 3.20- 5.84; exact p=7.8x10-4), without increased baseline activity. Parametric predictive checks exposed residual Poisson overdispersion; fixed-decay and beta-binomial sensitivity analyses nevertheless preserved the mutant history effect. Median %[eta] separated all 13 held-out assembloids, while a multifeature recording-level RBF-SVM achieved AUC 0.816 under nested whole-assembloid holdout. These results identify robust history-dependent temporal amplification as a functional MAPT-mutant network phenotype.

raw_data.title: Direction-sensitive neural correlates of voluntary pain regulation: regional response attenuation during down-regulation and exploratory prefrontal-valuation coupling
raw_data.abstract: Voluntary cognitive regulation can increase or decrease pain, but direction-sensitive neural correlates may emerge at different analytical levels. We reanalyzed 3,201 thermal-stimulation trials from 33 participants, integrating 0-200 warmth/pain ratings, regional fMRI activity, and trial-wise lagged coupling. Both instructions shifted ratings in the intended direction, with no reliable difference in mean success. Down-regulation was associated with lower bilateral S2/opercular and insular activity and higher left dlPFC/IFJ activity after FDR correction across 32 regions; run-matched comparisons were weaker and none survived the corresponding correction. Contrast-map Neurologic Pain Signature attenuation did not replicate in a rating-adjusted FWL-LSS trial-wise analysis despite strong temperature sensitivity. Up-regulation success covaried with an exploratory, post selection lagged dlPFC/IFJ-valuation composite (r = -0.546, 95% CI [-0.764, -0.270]). The association exceeded matched reverse-direction, zero-lag, and time-reversed controls, lay outside permutation and circular-shift nulls, and persisted after AR(1) prewhitening. A transition-level analysis across 297 up-regulation transitions preserved a negative success-by-source interaction (adjusted three-target mean beta = -0.163, cluster-bootstrap 95% CI [-0.290, -0.054], Freedman-Lane p = 0.010). Six session-wise DCM variants showed no consistent regulation-versus-passive effective-connectivity effect and did not independently validate an up-specific directed mechanism. These analyses identify a down-regulation-associated regional pattern and a candidate prefrontal-valuation coupling association requiring independent confirmation.

raw_data.title: Larger Pre-Speech Auditory Modulation Is Associated With Smaller Corrective Responses To Auditory Errors
raw_data.abstract:
PurposeDuring speech planning, the brain predicts the auditory consequences of its movements and modulates the auditory system--a process called pre-speech auditory modulation (PSAM). We investigated the link between PSAM and behavioral error correction and determined how aging influences these mechanisms.

MethodsSeventeen young adults (18-32 years) and 13 older adults (50-85 years) performed a speaking task involving auditory feedback perturbations and a silent reading control. We measured electrophysiological responses (N1/P2) to auditory probes during speech planning and correlated these modulations with the magnitude of participants subsequent behavioral corrective responses.

ResultsBoth groups showed significant modulation of N1 and P2. However, N1 modulation correlated with corrective responses only in young adults. Older adults showed reduced behavioral corrections and smaller, delayed P2 components. Despite these age-related behavioral differences and the loss of the modulation-correction correlation, older adults maintained modulation magnitudes comparable to those of younger adults.

ConclusionsN1 modulation serves as a neural index of the brains predictive processes during speech planning. Aging appears to selectively disrupt the integration of these signals into motor output rather than the internal generation of the predictions themselves.

raw_data.title: DNA polymerase kappa supports repair-associated DNA synthesis and neuronal genome resilience
raw_data.abstract:
Postmitotic neurons must preserve genome integrity for decades despite continuous oxidative, transcription-associated, and environmental DNA damage. Although recent studies have established ongoing repair-associated DNA synthesis in mature neurons, the polymerases that execute this synthesis remain incompletely defined. DNA polymerase kappa (POLK), a Y-family translesion synthesis polymerase, is highly expressed in neurons and undergoes an age-associated redistribution from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, suggesting that loss of nuclear POLK may compromise neuronal genome maintenance. Here, we investigated the consequences of POLK loss and augmentation in primary mouse cortical neurons and human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived forebrain neurons, including APOE e4/e4 backgrounds.

Partial POLK depletion reduced neuronal arbor complexity, enlarged neuronal nuclei, increased LAMIN A/C and nuclear-envelope abnormalities, and induced a multidimensional senescence-like stress phenotype characterized by increased senescence-associated {beta}-galactosidase, p21, nuclear p38 MAPK, inflammatory signaling, lysosomal remodeling, and reduced mitochondrial-associated staining. POLK localized in proximity to EdU-labeled DNA in mature neurons, and POLK depletion reproducibly reduced EdU incorporation across independent human neuronal backgrounds and maturation stages. Exploratory nuclear POLK immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, together with proximity ligation assays, placed POLK near proteins involved in nucleotide excision repair, base-excision/single-strand break repair, DNA-end repair, checkpoint signaling, and specialized polymerase regulation, including PCNA-Ub and RAD18.

POLK loss also produced Alzheimer disease-relevant cellular phenotypes. In wild-type neurons, POLK depletion increased 6E10 immunoreactivity and was accompanied by remodeling of APP/endosomal, lipid/cholesterol, and lysosomal pathways. In APOE e4/e4 neurons, POLK depletion increased cytoplasmic dsDNA and phospho-tau. Conversely, neuron-directed POLK augmentation increased EdU incorporation while reducing 53BP1 and {gamma}H2AX signals, p38 MAPK, cytoplasmic dsDNA, 6E10 immunoreactivity, and phospho-tau.

Together, these findings identify POLK as a component of repair-associated DNA synthesis in mature neurons and support a model in which neuronal POLK availability contributes to genome maintenance, stress resilience, and vulnerability in aging and Alzheimer disease-relevant states.

raw_data.title: Metabolite Relaxation Times at 3T From Birth to 7 Years
raw_data.abstract:
PurposeWith growing interest in pediatric MRS to understand the neurochemistry of brain development, it is essential to establish pediatric-specific metabolite T1 and T2 relaxation times for reliable quantification of metabolites. Furthermore, characterization of age-related changes in relaxation times may provide insight into developmental differences in tissue microstructure and cellular composition. Therefore, the goals of this study were two-fold: (1) to estimate metabolite T1 and T2 relaxation times in a pediatric cohort; and (2) to assess linear relationships between age and relaxation times.

MethodsTI- and TE-series data were acquired from the bilateral thalamus in 20 and 25 participants aged between 0 and 7 years, respectively. Data were processed and modelled in Osprey 2.5.0. Metabolite T1 and T2 relaxation times of total N-acetylaspartate at 2.0 ppm (tNAA2.0), total creatine at 3.0 ppm (tCr3.0), total creatine at 3.9 ppm (tCr3.9), total choline (tCho), myo-inositol (mI) and the combined glutamate and glutamine (Glx) were estimated by fitting the modelled signal amplitudes to TI-series inversion recovery signal and TE-series exponential decay equations, respectively. Linear relationships with age were tested for metabolite T1 and T2 relaxation times using Spearman correlations.

ResultstNAA2.0 and Glx showed significant changes in T1 with age. tNAA2.0, tCr3.0, tCho and mI showed significant decrease in T2 with age.

ConclusionSeveral metabolites showed significant changes in relaxation times with age in the thalamus region. Therefore, use of age-specific relaxation correction for pediatric studies using the linear equations provided is encouraged for reliable quantification of metabolites.

raw_data.title: Thalamocortical credit routing from the basal ganglia and cerebellum: anatomical constraints and circuit principles
raw_data.abstract: Animals learn to select actions that maximize reward in complex environments. A central challenge in this process is credit routing: behavioral outcomes must be routed back to the neural populations that contributed to generating the relevant actions. One possible route is through thalamocortical pathways conveying learning signals from the basal ganglia and cerebellum, where plasticity is shaped by reward-prediction errors. However, how these pathways route such signals back to specific cortical circuits remains unclear. To address this question, we combined anatomical circuit mapping in mice with closed-loop circuit modeling. Anterograde transsynaptic tracing revealed that thalamic neurons receiving input from the substantia nigra pars reticulata or the lateral cerebellar nucleus were largely segregated, with partial overlap in the ventromedial thalamus. Nevertheless, their cortical axons shared a pronounced enrichment in layer 1a, most prominently in secondary motor cortex. In a brain- wide synergistic loop-circuit model, learning was enhanced when both pathways delivered additive and gain-modulating feedback aligned with the cortical action readout. Local activity- based calibration established this alignment, whereas dendritic-spike- and reward-prediction- error-dependent thalamocortical plasticity further refined behavioral output. Module-specific feedback was essential for a brain-machine interface task requiring the simultaneous conditioning of multiple target neurons. Together, these findings define a credit-routing architecture in which laminar convergence, plastic alignment, and modular feedback link parallel subcortical learning systems to cortical action representations.

raw_data.title: Focal drug uncaging for the precise control of endogenous nicotinic receptors in behaving mice
raw_data.abstract: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptors shape diverse brain functions, including reward, aversion, and pain, but dissecting their roles in vivo requires drug delivery with spatiotemporal precision that conventional pharmacology cannot provide. Here we establish in vivo photopharmacology of endogenous nicotinic receptors: two complementary, highly-potent agonists, administered systemically in an inactive caged form, are photoreleased locally in target brain circuits of behaving wild-type mice. Despite irreversible photochemistry, photoactivation can be repeated over many trials on a minute timescale, for hours following a single injection. Local uncaging evokes circuit-specific dopamine release, drives place preference from the ventral tegmental area and aversion from the interpeduncular nucleus, and, in pain circuits, reveals a pronociceptive effect masked when the same agonists are given systemically. By controlling where and when nicotinic signaling acts, this approach exposes circuit-specific drug effects invisible to conventional pharmacology, and outlines a general strategy for on-demand control of endogenous receptors in vivo.

raw_data.title: Motivational incentives improve working memory performance by enhancing memory-based representations rather than altering response strategies
raw_data.abstract: Motivational incentives are known to improve working memory (WM) when items differ in value, but whether they enhance performance when all items are equally valued, and if so, by what mechanism, remains unclear. Improvements could reflect enhanced memory-based representations or speed-accuracy trade-offs, whereby incentives promote slower, more cautious responding without improving memory itself. Here, we tested these alternatives across two experiments using an auditory WM task in which incentives varied across trials, but all items on a trial were equally incentivised. In Experiment 1,we allowed participants to resubmit their responses if desired. Reward-related improvements in WM performance were selectively observed when memory load was high, and only at serial positions associated with greater interference. These improvements were also dissociated from systematic response slowing and resubmission behaviour. This indicated that the benefits of incentives were unlikely to be attributable to response caution. Critically, in Experiment 2, motivational benefits persisted under strict response deadlines, where speed cannot be traded for accuracy. Computational modelling showed that reward selectively improved the precision of memory-based responses without reducing guessing. Together, these findings indicate that motivational incentives improve WM by enhancing the quality of memory-based representations, rather than by strategic slowing or altering response strategies.

raw_data.title: Stage-specific proteomic signatures of synaptopathy in Alzheimers disease
raw_data.abstract:
Synapse loss is the strongest pathological correlate of cognitive decline in Alzheimers disease, yet the molecular basis of synaptic vulnerability across disease progression remains poorly understood.

We performed proteomic profiling of isolated synaptoneurosomes from post-mortem middle temporal gyrus tissue from 67 individuals, comprising 40 individuals spanning all Alzheimers disease Braak stages and 27 non-diseased controls. Differential abundance and weighted gene co-expression network analyses were combined with pathway, cell-type and gene set variation analyses to characterise stage-associated changes in the synaptic proteome. Brain-derived candidate proteins were subsequently evaluated using receiver operating characteristic and regression analyses against cognitive examination scores in two independent plasma proteomics datasets.

We identified six distinct stage-associated synaptic proteomic signatures. Mitochondrial function and synaptic signalling declined by mid-stage Alzheimers disease, while clathrin-mediated endocytosis increased at mid-stage without further change at later stages. By contrast, proteostasis and perisynaptic astrocytic processes increased progressively throughout the disease course. Global excitatory and inhibitory protein signals also showed a progressive shift in their relative balance (P = 7.80 x 10-3; adjusted R{superscript 2} = 0.072). These findings guided targeted investigation of candidate plasma markers linked to distinct synaptic processes in two independent proteomic datasets. We nominated 42 plasma proteins mapping to synaptic signatures of progression, which showed associations with disease stage and cognitive measures including Mini-Mental State Examination, Montreal Cognitive Assessment and Clinical Dementia Rating. PHGDH was prioritised across analyses through associations with cognitive impairment from early disease stages (Clinical Dementia Rating transition 0 to 0.5, false discovery rate = 8.87 x 10-18), neuropathological progression (P = 6.85 x 10-7) and excitatory-inhibitory protein imbalance (P = 5.56 x 10-3).

Together, our findings define the stage-associated molecular changes at the AD synapse and connect distinct brain pathways to accessible plasma candidates, establishing a mechanistically anchored framework for future patient stratification and evaluation of synapse-directed therapies.
